state.title: docs/cmdline-opts/write-out.d

part.text:
Yes — curl supports `-w "%{json}"`. It emits a JSON object containing all the available write-out keys.

## Supporting commit

**`04c03416e68fd635a15cae8201872f5c29fdcca8`** — *"writeout: support to generate JSON output"*, authored by Mathias Gumz, Sat Feb 1 2020, `Closes #4870`. It is an ancestor of the pinned `HEAD` (`ee521a1c8`), and the `%{json}` key is still present in the current tree (`docs/cmdline-opts/write-out.d:85`).

The commit message states the feature directly:

```
writeout: support to generate JSON output

This commit adds support to generate JSON via the writeout feature:

    -w "%{json}"

It leverages the existing infrastructure as much as possible. Thus,
generating the JSON on STDERR is possible by:

    -w "%{stderr}%{json}"

This implements a variant of
https://github.com/curl/curl/wiki/JSON#--write-out-json.

Closes #4870
```

The diff adds the documentation key in `docs/cmdline-opts/write-out.d`:

```diff
+.B json
+A JSON object with all available keys.
```

and implements it in a new file `src/tool_writeout_json.c` (181 lines) plus `src/tool_writeout_json.h`, wired into `src/tool_writeout.c`, `src/Makefile.inc`, and `lib/version.c`.

So your recollection is correct: `-w "%{json}"` is real, and it produces a single JSON object holding every available write-out value. You can also route it to stderr with `-w "%{stderr}%{json}"`.

(No files were modified.)
